note: One primitive camping spot: a gravel turnaround lot with a small grassy opening beside it, in timber at the foot of the bluff where County Road 350 reaches the Mississippi bottoms. A railroad line passes about 15 m from the spot. The river is roughly 250 m away across the tracks and an open bottomland field and is not in view. The road in is cut off when the Mississippi is over 20 feet on the Chester gauge. No pads, tables, privy or water. --Claude
summary: Confirmed: MDC 'Designated Camping Sites' - one Primitive Camping symbol beside a Parking Lot symbol on the map and one GIS camping point, 22 m from a gravel turnaround lot. Free, FCFS, no hookups, 14-day limit. Phone matches the area page. Pin is on the camping point beside the lot; it stays. Not waterfront stands. The only access warning is the river-stage one.
flags: INCLUSION (lot rule - stays, thin): the area page lists 'Camping: Designated Camping Sites'; the brochure's only camping line is 'Campers are limited to 14 consecutive days in a 30-day period. Groups of 10 or more campers need a special use permit.' The map (1/30/2024) draws one Primitive Camping symbol directly beside a Parking Lot symbol where the county road reaches the railroad; GIS layer 27 has one 'Primitive Camping Area' point (OBJECTID 407). On the 160 m leaf-off frame it is a gravel turnaround about 30 m across under bare trees with a grassy opening about 15 x 10 m on its north-west side where the GIS point sits, and one vehicle parked at the lot edge. No pads, privy or tables are visible. MDC marks a designated point at the lot, so it stays under the 2026-11-09 rule; in practice a motorhome camps on the turnaround. A 23-ft rig fits it.

ACCESS WARNING, in full: the area page and the brochure both say only 'Red Rock Landing Conservation Area is inaccessible by road when the Mississippi River level is over 20 feet on the Chester Power gauge.' Nothing on the page, brochure or map mentions a railroad crossing restriction, a levee gate, a private road, 4WD or a posted limit. Directions: 'From Perryville, take Highway 61 south, then Route P east, then Route C north, and at Crosstown take County Road 350 east to the area.' The map shows County Road 350 as a 'Non-MDC Road' running to the lot and on across the railroad to the river bottom; the camping lot is on the near (bluff) side of the tracks, so a rig does not cross the railroad to reach it. In ordinary river stages a 23-ft motorhome reaches the lot on the county road as far as these sources show; I could not read the road's surface or grades (OSM was unread - the Overpass mirror timed out - and the leaf-off frame shows only a narrow lane under trees). 20 ft at Chester is below that gauge's flood stage, so the cut-off will come most springs; I did not look up stage statistics.

RIVER: the lot is about 250 m from the Mississippi bank on the 900 m frame, with the railroad embankment, an open bottomland field and a band of bank timber between. Nothing of the river is seen from the camping spot. Stored not waterfront stands.
RAILROAD: the main line passes about 15 m north of the camping point (written into the note as a caveat).

PIN: stored 37.74866,-89.66981 is GIS point 407 on the grassy opening beside the lot (GIS lot 725 at 37.74852,-89.66965, 22 m). No move. The area's second lot (37.74689,-89.67130, 240 m south-west up the road) has no camping symbol.
PHONE: stored 573-290-5730 matches the area page's 'For more information call (573) 290-5730'.
SEASON: stored year_round (manual) stands; no camping season is given.
